niche.title: The Worst Ideas in the History of Medicine, Ranked
niche.description:
In London in 1780, a drowned man could be treated with a kit from a wooden box on the riverbank: a pair of bellows, a tube and a tin of tobacco, to blow smoke up his backside. That is only number five on this countdown of the worst medical ideas in history, ranked by how sure the doctors were against how badly it went. Along the way come heroin sold by Bayer for coughs and about five pints of blood taken from George Washington in twelve hours.

niche.title: How Is Spinal Anesthesia Given? 💉3D Animation | How Doctors Give Spinal Anesthesia Before Surgery
niche.description:
How is spinal anesthesia given? 💉 Watch this 3D medical animation to understand how doctors administer spinal anesthesia before certain surgical procedures.

The animation explains how the doctor cleans the lower back, identifies the L3–L4 vertebral space, administers anesthetic medication into the cerebrospinal fluid space, and checks for numbness in the lower body.

Spinal anesthesia is commonly used for procedures such as C-sections and certain surgeries involving the lower body.

niche.title: What Did People Do Before ANESTHESIA?
niche.description:
Before anesthesia, surgery hurt. A lot. So surgeons got fast: London surgeon Robert Liston could take off a leg in about two and a half minutes while students timed him with pocket watches. Meanwhile laughing gas was a party trick, and in 1844 a dentist named Horace Wells watched a man smash his leg at a laughing-gas show and feel nothing. Guess in the comments: whose tooth got pulled first? Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace_Wells

niche.title: Anesthesia 🧠: What Happens to Your Brain During Surgery?
niche.description:
Anesthesia doesn't simply switch your brain off. It temporarily changes how different parts of your brain communicate. 🧠

You close your eyes, and when you wake up, the surgery may already be over. But what happens inside your body during that time? Let's understand the science behind general anesthesia.

💉 1. Propofol: The Drug That Helps You Lose Consciousness

Propofol is a commonly used general anesthetic. It enhances the activity of GABA, a chemical messenger that reduces activity in the nervous system.

This changes communication between brain networks, helping produce unconsciousness.

niche.title: World Anaesthesia Day: Why Is PAC Important Before Surgery? | Dr Sumanth Kankanala
niche.description:
What is Pre-Anaesthetic Evaluation (PAC), and why is it essential before surgery? 🩺

On the occasion of World Anaesthesia Day, Dr Sumanth Kankanala, Chief of Anesthesiology at Continental Hospitals, Hyderabad, explains the importance of Pre-Anaesthetic Check-up (PAC) and how it helps identify potential risks before anesthesia and surgery.

A pre-anesthetic evaluation is a detailed assessment performed by an anesthesiologist before surgery to understand the patient's medical condition, evaluate possible complications, and plan anesthesia safely.
